messages: ana: Quick design check — thinking through the compact 'inspector' that appears when you click a version on the rollout timeline. I pushed a small mock to Figma. Thoughts on hover vs persistent focus state for keyboard users? mike: Saw it — nice tight layout. Concern: when the inspector is compact it packs info into small chips; hover reveals details. But we need keyboard parity. How do we expose the same detail on focus? sam: Agree about parity. Implementation note: we can trigger the same expansion on :focus-within and have a `aria-expanded` attribute on the inspector container. But we should avoid accidental expansions with tabbing through. yvonne: Accessibility nit: please ensure hover-only tooltips are not the only way to get context. For screen reader users, we should have an `aria-describedby` pointer to a hidden region that reads the chip details on focus. Also contrast on the micro-pill labels is only 3.2:1 — needs to be 4.5:1 for body text. ana: Good call. For keyboard, proposal: single Tab lands on the version node (same as today), Enter opens the inspector; within inspector arrow keys navigate chips and space toggles chip expansion. Hover still expands for mouse. This keeps tab order minimal. mike: I like Enter to open. But product concern: many users expect a quick hover peek without full open. Can we support a transient hover preview (no focus) and a persistent open on click/Enter? sam: Technically doable: two layers — a transient `:hover` preview (CSS transform + opacity), and a JS-driven persistent inspector with `role="dialog"` when opened. Preview should be detach-only and not steal focus. yvonne: If adding `role="dialog"` we need to ensure focus is trapped when open and `aria-modal` applied only if it truly blocks interaction. This inspector is contextual, not modal — so don't use `aria-modal=true`. Instead, manage focus return on close. mike: Copy nit: the pill that shows allocation currently reads "canary: 5%" — can we make it "Canary — 5% traffic" for clarity in the compact view? Tests showed users misread numbers as version ids. ana: Ok, we can update microcopy. Also adding a visually hidden label for screen readers: `Canary variant, receiving 5 percent of traffic`. sam: CSS snippet for hover preview (very small): ```css .rollout-node .preview { transform: translateY(-6px); opacity: 0; transition: opacity .12s ease, transform .12s ease; } .rollout-node:hover .preview { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } ``` sam: For keyboard focus we do: `:focus-within .preview { opacity: 1; }` but only if the node itself is focused (so users tab to it). yvonne: Also: avoid hover previews that disappear too fast. Add a 200ms delay before hiding so users with motor difficulties can move pointer into the preview. But ensure it doesn't interfere with quick hover impressions. mike: UX question: when a user opens the inspector, do we show a "Revert" CTA inline or only in the expanded version history? Inline "Revert" lets quick rollbacks but might cause accidental clicks. Thoughts? ana: My vote: show a low-prominence inline "Undo" icon (danger outline style) in compact inspector, but require a confirmation modal for the actual rollback. That keeps quick access without accidental immediate action. sam: Implementation: the inline action can be a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` that triggers the rollback confirmation. Keeps semantics clear. yvonne: Ensure the confirmation modal has clear instructions and an accessible descriptive label. Use `role=dialog` and `aria-labelledby` + `aria-describedby`. Focus should move into modal. deploy-bot: deploy status update: next staging deploy with the compact inspector toggles goes out tomorrow at 1500UTC. Watch `rollout-inspector` feature flag. :rocket: ana: Thanks — I'll update Figma to reflect the keyboard flow, copy changes, and the contrast adjustments. Will add notes on timing (200ms hide delay) and the `aria-describedby` implementation. mike: One last tiny thing — micro-pill spacing: reduce horizontal padding by 2px to avoid wrapping on narrow sidebars. But keep touch target >=44px for mobile breakpoints. yvonne: Confirming: for touch, we should avoid hover previews entirely and rely on tap to open. Document that in the pattern. an a: Great. I'll post the updated frames + a short checklist for engineering: 1) hover preview CSS + 200ms hide, 2) Enter opens persistent inspector (role=dialog), 3) keyboard arrow navigation inside chips, 4) sr-only descriptive text for pills, 5) confirm modal semantics, 6) update microcopy to "Canary — 5% traffic", 7) contrast & padding fixes. mike: Perfect. We can close this thread once the PR references the checklist. :thumbsup:
